article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Big Buddha Cheese × NYC Diesel
Breeder: Big Buddha Seeds
THC Content: 20-27%
CBD Content: 0.08%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , linalool , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Cheese, diesel fuel, grapefruit, spice, hash
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October to early November
Indoor Yield: 400 g+
Outdoor Yield: 1,200 g+ per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Some cannabis crosses are memorable because they soften the extremes of their parents. Chiesel does almost the opposite. Big Buddha Seeds took two of the loudest flavor families of their era—British Cheese and Soma’s NYC Diesel—and deliberately pushed them together. The resulting weed carries the sour, greasy pungency of Cheese alongside grapefruit, fuel and spice from the Diesel side, producing an aromatic profile that is difficult to mistake for a mild modern hybrid. Big Buddha Seeds dates the creation to around 2008 and describes the cultivar as a 60% sativa, 40% indica hybrid bred from Big Buddha Cheese and a male NYC Diesel selected from Soma’s genetics. The breeder gives it an indoor flowering period of eight to ten weeks and describes the effect as clear, uplifting and unusually long lasting.

Chiesel also represents an important meeting point between two different cannabis cultures. Cheese grew out of the British fascination with an exceptionally pungent Skunk-derived clone, while NYC Diesel became associated with Soma ‘s Amsterdam breeding work and its unmistakable citrus-fuel profile. Big Buddha’s version does not hide either side. Plants can display the narrower, more elongated appearance expected from a sativa-leaning hybrid, yet the Cheese influence keeps flowers substantial and the flowering period relatively manageable. The result is marijuana that feels distinctly old-school without being sleepy or one-dimensional: pungent enough for devoted Cheese fans, acidic enough for Diesel enthusiasts, and mentally energetic enough to separate it from many heavier European hybrids.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed formula is Big Buddha Cheese × NYC Diesel, with the NYC Diesel used as the male parent. Big Buddha Seeds specifically credits Soma for that male, stating that the Diesel selection supplied hybrid vigor along with its characteristic grapefruit-diesel flavor. The breeder lists the finished genetic balance at approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica. Although Chiesel’s name makes the combination obvious, the breeding history behind the Cheese side deserves attention because it explains why the resulting cultivar is more complex than a simple Skunk × Diesel pairing.

Big Buddha Cheese traces to the famous UK Cheese clone. Big Buddha Seeds describes its early breeding program as beginning around 2000 with a clone-only Skunk No. 1 female crossed to a selected Afghani male, followed by extensive selection and backcrossing. By 2002 the breeder had developed a seed form of Cheese designed to retain the intense aroma of the clone while adding yield and stability. The strain later won the Best Indica Seed category at the 2006 High Times Cannabis Cup , helping establish Big Buddha Cheese internationally. That foundation contributes much of Chiesel’s skunky dairy pungency, resin production and comparatively robust flower formation.

NYC Diesel pulls the hybrid in another direction. Its grapefruit-citrus character, fuel aroma and more expansive mental effect give Chiesel a brighter personality than Big Buddha Cheese alone. Big Buddha Seeds describes the offspring as growing similarly to its Cheese mother but with a slender, fast-flowering sativa appearance and underlying indica traits. The combination therefore works on several levels: Cheese adds dankness and body, Diesel contributes vigor and acidic fruit, and both parents reinforce the pungent aromatic intensity that defines the finished cultivar.
Effects and Experience

Chiesel typically makes its presence felt first in the head. The onset can be quick and mentally elevating, with attention becoming sharper and mood moving upward before substantial physical heaviness develops. Big Buddha Seeds describes the effect as highly uplifting, clear and long lasting, emphasizing that it does not readily hit an obvious ceiling. In practical terms, moderate amounts can feel energetic without necessarily becoming frantic. Conversation may flow more easily, music can become unusually absorbing and routine activities may feel more interesting than they did beforehand.

Physical relaxation gradually fills in beneath that cerebral lift. The Cheese ancestry contributes enough indica character to prevent the experience from feeling like a narrow, edgy sativa, but the body component usually does not dominate early. This balance helps explain Chiesel’s enduring reputation as relatively functional weed for experienced consumers. Depending on dose and tolerance, the middle portion of the experience can combine euphoria, focus and sociability with a steady easing of muscular tension. Later, larger doses may become significantly heavier, especially when modern batches test well above 20% THC.

Potency deserves particular attention because contemporary Chiesel can be considerably stronger than strains commonly available when the genetics first appeared. One regulated Florida flower batch analyzed by ACS Laboratory measured 27.3% total active THC and only 0.075% total active CBD, while an Arizona Chiesel pre-roll analyzed by Green Scientific Labs measured approximately 21.2% total THC. These are individual products rather than universal strain standards, but they illustrate the possible range. Someone unfamiliar with potent marijuana may encounter anxiety, dry mouth, dizziness, impaired attention or an uncomfortably intense cerebral rush if the dose is too large.
Medical Benefits

Chiesel’s combination of mental elevation and later physical relaxation makes it understandable why some medical cannabis patients gravitate toward similar THC-dominant hybrids. The brighter opening may be preferable to a strongly sedating cultivar for people who want to remain engaged during the day, while the underlying body calm may appeal to patients dealing with persistent discomfort or physical tension. Appetite stimulation and mood elevation are also commonly associated with THC-rich marijuana, although the experience varies significantly from one individual to another.

None of those potential uses should be treated as proof that Chiesel itself treats a medical condition. Clinical research generally examines cannabinoids or standardized cannabis preparations rather than named commercial cannabis strains . The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that evidence suggests modest benefits from cannabis or cannabinoids for some chronic-pain conditions and certain symptoms of multiple sclerosis, while evidence for many other uses remains limited or uncertain. NCCIH also emphasizes that the cannabis plant itself has not been approved by the FDA as a medical treatment, although several cannabinoid-based prescription drugs have been approved for specific indications.

The strain’s high THC potential also creates reasons for caution. THC can impair coordination, reaction time and judgment, and some people experience anxiety, rapid heart rate, dizziness or pronounced sedation after larger doses. Cannabis can additionally interact with medications. A medical marijuana patient is better served by reviewing the cannabinoid and terpene analysis of a specific batch—and discussing use with a qualified healthcare professional when appropriate—than assuming every flower sold as Chiesel will produce the same result.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Chiesel’s aroma is not subtle. The Cheese parent contributes the unmistakable combination of sour dairy, skunk, musk and fermented pungency associated with classic British Cheese genetics. NYC Diesel then cuts through that heaviness with fuel and grapefruit. Big Buddha Seeds summarizes the smell as Cheese mixed with Diesel and describes the flavor more specifically as spicy grapefruit and hash. When the flowers are broken apart, these elements can overlap into an almost industrial aroma: sharp citrus rind, petrol, funky cheese and dark resin.

On the inhale, fuel and citrus often arrive before the heavier Cheese side becomes obvious. Grapefruit supplies acidity rather than simple sweetness, while peppery spice and hash can develop toward the finish. Properly cured flower may also reveal earthy, herbal or faintly floral notes beneath the dominant funk. The profile is considerably more savory than today’s candy-oriented weed, and consumers who appreciate classic Cheese, Skunk or Diesel varieties are more likely to view its aggressive aroma as a strength rather than a flaw.

Modern laboratory results provide some chemical context without establishing a universal terpene formula. A 2024 ACS Laboratory analysis of a Florida Chiesel batch measured 1.424% total terpenes, led by trans-caryophyllene at 0.442%, followed by linalool, beta-myrcene, alpha-bisabolol, alpha-humulene and smaller amounts of limonene. That particular sample helps explain the strain’s combination of pepper, floral-herbal depth and earthy pungency, but terpene percentages should never be treated as fixed genetic constants. Phenotype, lighting, nutrition, harvest timing, drying and storage can all change the finished aromatic profile.
Growing Information

Chiesel develops with a structure that reflects both sides of its lineage. Big Buddha Seeds describes it as relatively slender and sativa-looking while retaining indica characteristics inherited from Cheese. Plants may stretch noticeably when flowering begins, so indoor gardens benefit from planning vertical space before the photoperiod changes. Branching can become vigorous, particularly in Diesel-leaning phenotypes, and the combination of lateral development and substantial flower production makes an even canopy useful for taking advantage of available light.

The breeder lists an indoor flowering period of eight to ten weeks and places outdoor maturity from late October into early November. Indoor production is listed at 400 g or more, while outdoor plants are advertised as capable of exceeding 1,200 g under favorable circumstances. The current breeder page does not present those figures in the same standardized grams-per-square-meter format used by some seed catalogs, so they are best treated as breeder yield estimates rather than guaranteed measurements. Environmental conditions, plant size, light intensity and phenotype will have a major influence on actual production.

A moderate difficulty rating fits the cultivar well. Chiesel is vigorous rather than notoriously fragile, but its stretch, strong odor and extended outdoor finish require planning. Branches carrying mature flowers may benefit from support late in bloom, and adequate airflow becomes increasingly important as flower density builds. Odor control can also be a serious consideration indoors because the combination of Cheese and Diesel produces an exceptionally conspicuous smell. Outdoors, the late-October to early-November finish favors climates with relatively dry autumn weather; extended cold rain can become problematic as dense resinous flowers approach maturity.
FAQ
Is Chiesel an indica or sativa?

Chiesel is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Big Buddha Seeds officially lists the strain as approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica. Its effects generally begin with an uplifting cerebral component before more noticeable physical relaxation develops.
What are the genetics of Chiesel?
The original lineage is Big Buddha Cheese × NYC Diesel. Big Buddha Seeds used its own Cheese as the female parent and an NYC Diesel male originating from Soma’s genetics as the pollen parent.
How much THC does Chiesel have?

There is no single breeder-established THC percentage. Modern laboratory-tested examples demonstrate considerable potency variation: one regulated sample tested at approximately 21.2% total THC, while another flower batch reached 27.3% total active THC.
What does the Chiesel strain taste like?

Expect a pungent combination of cheese, diesel fuel, grapefruit, spice and hash. The Cheese parent supplies much of the funky, savory aroma, while NYC Diesel contributes the sharp citrus-fuel component.
How long does Chiesel take to flower?

Big Buddha Seeds gives Chiesel an indoor flowering period of eight to ten weeks. Outdoor plants typically mature from late October into early November in climates capable of supporting the full flowering cycle.
Final Thoughts on Chiesel

Chiesel succeeds because neither parent disappears inside the cross. Big Buddha Cheese remains obvious in the musky, sour and intensely pungent side of the flowers, while NYC Diesel supplies grapefruit, fuel and much of the strain’s cerebral energy. Instead of averaging those qualities into something mild, Big Buddha Seeds produced marijuana that magnifies them. The resulting 60/40 hybrid can be uplifting and surprisingly functional while still carrying enough indica influence to provide a substantial physical finish.

Its history also gives Chiesel continuing relevance in a market increasingly dominated by descendants of a smaller number of dessert-oriented genetic families. Big Buddha Seeds created the cultivar around 2008 from two already established strains, and the breeder continues to maintain Chiesel in its catalog today. For anyone interested in classic Cheese or Diesel weed, that continuity matters. Chiesel remains an unusually direct expression of both traditions: sharp grapefruit against fermented Cheese funk, powerful THC potential, energetic hybrid effects and an aroma strong enough to announce the harvest well before the jar is opened.
